The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 01.02.2024.
2.

The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 01.02.2024 at about 03.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding the Scooter bearing Reg. No. MH-12-PP-6694 along with his wife as pillion rider on Hagadur Main Road, slowly and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations and by wearing head-guard, when they reached infront Dr. Batra Dental Care Clinic Road, at that time one Water Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-51-C-0633 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came at high speed from same direction from left side of the petitioner Scooter at high speed and dashed against the handle of the petitioner Scooter.

Due to forced impact,
petitioner and pillion rider both fell down and right rear wheel of the Water Tanker ran over the left leg of the petitioner and pillion rider both sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.20,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 45 years, the petitioner was working as Software Engineer at VOIS INDIA Services Ltd.,
Marathahalli, Bangalore and earning Rs.25,00,000/- p.a.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and unable to look after the said work.
Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-
with interest.

sentences.text: After service of notice, both the respondents appeared through their counsels, but respondent No.1 failed to file his written statement.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and submitted that, this respondent issued the policy to the offending vehicle and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It is further submitted that, the driver of the Water Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA- 51-C-0633 was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of alleged accident.

The alleged accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, who was riding his Scooter without wearing head-guard and without holding valid and effective driving license to ride the Scooter as on the date of accident.

Respondent No.2 denies the occurrence of the accident and involvement of Water Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-51-C-0633 as the same is not within the knowledge of this respondent and insured in terms of the policy has not intimated the same.
Further this respondent denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the driver of Water Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-51-C-0633 at about 03.00 p.m., infront of Dr. Batra Dental Care Clinic Road, Hagaduru Main Road, Bangalore and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 26.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P.2 is the Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the Sketch, Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report,

Ex.P.6 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.7 is the C/c of MLC, Ex.P.8 is the Notice U/s 133 of M. V. Act,
Ex.P.9 is the Reply Notice, Ex.P.10 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P.11 to 13 are the Discharge Summaries,
Ex.P.14 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card of petitioner, Ex.P.15 is the Notarized copy of Driving License, Ex.P.16 is the bills, Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.21 are the Photos, Ex.P.22 is the receipt, Ex.P.23 is the Pen-drive, Ex.P.24 is the Payslips, Ex.P.25 is the Bank Statement, Ex.P.26 is the Medical Bill.
10.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving by the driver of Water Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-51-C-0633.
11.
Ex.P.1 to 10 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

The Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4 (spot panchanama and sketch), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.10, Charge-Sheet against the driver of offending vehicle U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC along with Sec.134(B) and 187 of M.
V. Act. The Ex.P.5 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles in question.
12. Learned counsel for petitioner contended that, the accident is caused due to rash and negligent act of driver of the offending vehicle.
Contesting respondent has not disputed the accident.
Except suggestions and denial insurance company has not produced any documents to show that, accident is caused due to the negligence of petitioner.

13. In view of the discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of rider of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Water Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-51-C-0633.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Manipal Hospital as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
15. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 01.02.2024 to 17.02.2024, again from 18.02.2024 to 09.03.2024 and again on 23.03.2024.

The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.13 wherein it is mentioned that the Rajesh Gangadharrao Thakare vs Revathi Sharmila A G on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91840822/

He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, which reveals that, petitioner has sustained following injuries,
(i) Major crush injury to left foot and ankle with mangled foot with doubtful vascularity of plantar skin.
(ii) multiple metatarsal and calcaneal fractures with degloving injury of foot and ankle.
(iii) fracture neck of femur left side.
and the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.75,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.

In support of his plea, he has produced 07 medical bills which is marked at Ex.P.16 to the tune of Rs.13,897/- and also produced 16 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.26 to the tune of Rs.4,47,829/-.

On going through the medical records it reveals that, petitioner admitted in the hospital for 03 times and further the petitioner has taken contention that, he has spent more than Rs.20,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.
But as per the records, the insurance company already paid Rs.98,385/- and patient has paid the balance amount of Rs.4,31,072/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,61,726/- towards medical expenses.

17. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 to 13 Discharge summaries issued by Manipal Hospital, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital for about 37 days.
Moreover, petitioner himself in his evidence depose that, he has not attended any work till 1st April 2024.
Hence, at least 02 month is required to recover from the accidental injuries.
It is further contended that, the injured petitioner was working as Software Engineer at VOIS INDIA Services Ltd., Marathahalli, Bangalore and earning Rs.25,00,000/- per annum.
In support of his plea he has produced the documents marked at Ex.P.24 Payslips.
In this case, in order to prove the salary, the petitioner has not examined his employer.
However, on going through the bank statement as well as pay slips produced by the petitioner, it reveals that, he was drawing salary of Rs.1,48,000/- per month.
Hence, 02 month is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,96,000/- under this head.

19. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Manipal Hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 01.02.2024 to 17.02.2024, again from 18.02.2024 to 09.03.2024 and again on 23.03.2024 i.e., for 37 days.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.
20. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 46 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that, he found difficulty in doing day to day works.
He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.
21. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has claimed towards future medical expenses.
The doctor who has been examined as PW.4 has suggested another surgery for removal of implants from left femur.
By keeping nature of the injuries sustained, as he is bound to suffer medical problems in future and cannot every time depend upon Government hospital.
Hence, under this head Rs.30,000/- is awarded.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 75,000/-
2 Medical expenses Rs. 4,61,726/-
3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 2,96,000/-
up period 4 Nutritious food and Rs. 60,000/-
attendant charges 5 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 50,000/-

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,72,726/- under various heads.
22. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Water Tanker bearing Reg. No. KA-51-C-0633 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC along with Sec.134(b) and 187 of M. V. Act.
Admittedly in its written statement Insurance company has not disputed the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle.
As per the written statement of respondent No.2, the offending vehicle was insured for the period from 12.03.2023 to 11.03.2024.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 01.02.2024.

Hence,
policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 owner.
23. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered partly in the affirmative.
24. ISSUE No.4:

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.9,72,726/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 60% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon.

Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.9,72,726/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 60% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon.
Remaining 40% of compensation amount of petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award Accordingly.
